Global News Summary - July 29, 2025

Breaking News

Manhattan Office Shooting Kills Four
Gunman Shane Tamura, 27, killed four people including an off-duty NYPD officer at Manhattan's 345 Park Avenue before taking his own life. Using an M4 rifle, he targeted NFL headquarters, leaving a note claiming brain trauma from football.

Beijing Floods Claim 30 Lives
Severe flooding killed 30 people in Beijing, with 80,000 evacuated. Miyun district recorded 21 inches of rainfall as rescue operations continue across the region with widespread power outages.

U.S. Exits Gaza Ceasefire Talks
Trump administration withdrew negotiators from Qatar, citing Hamas's bad faith. Special envoy Witkoff announced alternative options to secure hostage releases.

International Politics

Cambodia-Thailand Ceasefire Holds
Border fighting that killed 38 people ended with Trump-brokered ceasefire. Despite minor violations, truce remains intact as military commanders meet to solidify agreements.

Russian Strikes Kill 22 in Ukraine
Russian attacks killed 22 across Ukraine, including 17 prison inmates in Zaporizhzhia. Trump shortened Putin's peace deadline to 10-12 days, warning of sanctions.

Global Economics

U.S.-EU Trade Deal Reached
Agreement imposes 15% tariffs on EU goods, down from threatened 30%. EU commits $600 billion U.S. investment and $750 billion energy purchases through 2028, averting trade war.

Markets Mixed Before Fed Meeting
S&P 500 hit sixth straight record while Asian markets retreated. Dollar strengthened on trade progress as investors await Federal Reserve decision.

Natural Disasters

Philippines Typhoon Kills 25
Typhoon Co-may and monsoon rains killed 25, evacuated 278,000 people. Over 80 towns declared calamity states as flooding damaged 3,000 homes.

Science Developments

Virtual Scientists Advance Biology
Stanford researchers created AI-driven 'virtual scientists' to solve complex biological problems, designing nanobodies for potential COVID-19 vaccines that bind effectively to variants.

Artificial Cells Mimic Biological Clocks
UC Merced scientists engineered artificial cells that maintain 24-hour cycles, replicating living organisms' internal timing mechanisms.

Additional Developments

President Trump concluded Scotland visit opening Aberdeen golf course after meetings with UK PM Starmer and EU President von der Leyen. Global markets show cautious optimism with ongoing corporate earnings season. Regional conflicts continue affecting energy markets and diplomatic relations. Humanitarian assistance needed for Gaza and flood-affected regions.

data.text:
President Bongbong Marcos Jr. found his voice
 — his best State of the Nation Address yet!

As an avid supporter of the President, I follow the accomplishments of the Marcos administration — it is clear to me that we are in so much better hands now in all aspects of governance. No one can tell me that the President was not successful in his first three years in office because I have my data to back me up!

No administration is without any hiccup, this one has its fair share of them but President Marcos is smart and humble enough to learn from these unlikely circumstances. They say never mistake diplomacy as weakness — you will never find the President stooping down to the level those are against him but he will firmly demand accountability if it is affecting the lives of our kababayans.

Despite the political capital of the Villars as the head of a political party and influence in the business community, President Marcos stood his ground in saying that he is for the welfare of the six million Filipinos affected by their poor service. He said that LWUA will ensure that those who neglected and failed in this important public service are held accountable.

Mahiya naman kayo! In the first three years of the President, appropriations for projects that should have been the solution to a lot of our long-standing problems including the flooding. The call for accountability and the order of the President to investigate all substandard and ghost projects — there is nothing more evil than to enjoy money that is costing people their lives and quality of living.

No one will be protected! President Marcos will publish the list of the ghost and substandard projects, as he vows that the government will file criminal charges against those accountable within the next few months. 

There are rumors that one member of the 2025 bicameral conference committee said that if his insertions were not approved, he will delay the approval of the budget —- with the firm stance, the President said that he will not approve any line item that is not aligned with the direction of the National Government. Consequences be damned! As he would rather work with a reenacted budget than favor the benefits of one or two (lols!).

It is important to note that the House of Representatives acted on these the very next day, as the Speaker announced investigations of infrastructure projects — and the open budget deliberations from committee, plenary up to bicameral conference. To add, the larger house now opens the budget deliberations to civil society, academe and watchdogs for audit and monitor. 

The accomplishment of the Marcos Administration in health is something of note — healthcare is more accessible now than ever! He said that for the first time in Philippine history, every municipality in the Philippines has one dedicated doctor and in public health… This is a huge win.

If we improve primary care, we unclog government hospitals — giving way to patients who need hospital interventions the most! Then, we now have the best version of PhilHealth benefits and packages —- under the Marcos administration, PhilHealth expanded their benefits because they can and they should!

If the Fourth State of the Nation Address of President Marcos is any indication of what the next three years will be, the future of this country is brighter! 

Like for part 2!

data.text:
Severe storms and monsoon rains have recently battered the Philippines, causing widespread flooding, landslides, and the displacement of communities. Hundreds of thousands have been evacuated, and more than six dozen municipalities have declared a state of calamity. Schools and transportation services have been suspended in the affected areas, including Metro Manila. Tragically, lives have also been lost.

@ifrc is working closely with @philredcross. PRC has mobilized its nationwide volunteer network to support evacuations and deliver vital humanitarian assistance.

According to the latest reports from PRC, 38,892 people have received assistance through rescue operations, health and hygiene services, and the distribution of hot meals, relief items, and clean drinking water.
